01

Setting specification

Task

Find a feasible point of the monotone variational inequality whose tangential residual is at most $\varepsilon$. The normal cone describes the effect of the constraint set at the returned point.

Solve $0\in F(z)+N_K(z)$.

Admissible model

The set $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ is public, nonempty, closed, and convex, and may be unbounded. The operator $F$ is monotone and $\beta$-Lipschitz on $K$.

The initial point $z_0\in K$ is public, and a solution $z^\star$ satisfies $\|z_0-z^\star\|_2\le R$. The condition $\operatorname{diam}(K)\le R$ is not required.

Oracle interface

Public inputs include dimension $d$ and $R$, $\beta$, and $\varepsilon$, together with the stated initial points and feasible-set information. Analytic representations of hidden functions, operators, and matrices are not supplied.

$$ z\in K\longmapsto F(z) $$

Return the complete exact operator value, not one coordinate or a scalar function value.

Exact Euclidean projection onto the known set is allowed. Its calls are recorded separately and excluded from the primary query count.

Output

Return a feasible point $\widehat z\in K$.

The output may be any measurable postprocessing of the history, including an unqueried point, average, or convex combination. It must satisfy the stated domain and feasibility requirements; no additional function value or computable certificate is required.

Loss or accuracy criterion

Measure constrained stationarity by taking the smallest Euclidean norm of the operator value at the output plus a normal vector there. This residual must be at most $\varepsilon$ for each admissible instance.

$$ \operatorname{dist}(0,F(\widehat{z})+N_K(\widehat{z})) $$

For a closed convex set $K$, define $N_K(z)=\{v:\langle v,u-z\rangle\le0,\ \forall u\in K\}$ for $z\in K$, and $\operatorname{dist}(0,S)=\inf_{v\in S}\|v\|_2$.

The tangent residual is finite at feasible points because $0\in N_K(z)$. This metric is not equal to $\|F(z)\|_2$.

Resource accounting

Each complete operator-value call counts once in $N_{\rm operator}$; projection counts are recorded separately.

Use a fixed worst-case budget: calls never exceed the prespecified $N$ on any instance or random execution path. Earlier stopping within the budget is permitted.

Count all information calls for one instance and one requested accuracy, including initialization. Exact-real arithmetic, storage, and solving known models from public inputs and returned data are uncharged. This query-complexity quantity does not certify arithmetic or bit complexity.

Algorithm views and success guarantees

Any measurable sequential adaptive deterministic algorithm is allowed. Queries and outputs may use the complete history, with no additional span, zero-support, communication, or memory restriction.

The same deterministic algorithm must satisfy the guarantee for every admissible instance.

$$ \operatorname{dist}(0,F(\widehat{z})+N_K(\widehat{z}))\le\varepsilon. $$

Budget convention
fixed worst-case query cap

Halpern Iteration for Near-Optimal and Parameter-Free Monotone Inclusion and Strong Solutions to Variational Inequalities ↗
Conditions
Every condition in the eight-axis specification and associated regime must hold jointly. Sufficient constants from different theorems are not assumed identical.
Dimension conditions
Dimension $d\ge C\beta R/\varepsilon$ suffices. Complexity takes the worst case over all admissible finite dimensions.
Algorithm scope
Arbitrary deterministic adaptive algorithms; no randomized lower bound is asserted.
Correspondence, constants and qualifications
Oracle correspondence
Use only primitive operations recorded under ORACLE. Unknown inner solutions and reduced gradients are not supplied for free.
Guarantee conversion
The error criterion, sources of randomness, and expectation/probability quantifiers match this specification. Any conversion is explained separately below.
Output rule
Outputs belong to the declared space and are evaluated by this profile's METRIC. Different gaps, norms, and squared norms are not interchanged.
Resource conversion
All resource costs come from one algorithm or one hard construction. Initialization and nested calls are included.
Constants
Use the source theorem’s universal constants except where derivative order or structural budgets are explicitly fixed. Unspecified sufficient thresholds remain symbolic.
Logarithmic factors
None.
Derivation
The source hard domain can have diameter $R$, so any feasible public initial point is within $R$ of a solution. For every $v\in N_K(z)$, the local strong gap satisfies $\sup_{u\in K\cap B(z,1)}\langle F(z),z-u\rangle\le\|F(z)+v\|_2$, where $B(z,1)$ is the unit Euclidean ball centered at $z$. Taking the infimum over normal vectors converts the local-gap lower bound to a tangent-residual lower bound, preserving the quantifier over arbitrary deterministic algorithms.
Scope qualification
The source theorem covers arbitrary adaptive deterministic queries, beyond linear-span iterations. It does not thereby give an arbitrary-randomized lower bound.
Upper bound
\[O(\beta R/\varepsilon)\]
